name: Vendor Security Assessment
description: Questions a customer asks a software or SaaS provider before and during a contract: governance, access, data protection, secure development, operations and resilience. Written for Cerberus as an open, generic catalog; it reproduces no company's questionnaire. Each control can be answered by the provider and, where the scanner has a signal, judged from evidence.

methodology.overview: Every control gets a verdict and the evidence behind it. A control that is not met gets an action plan with a deadline.

controls.title: Security ownership
controls.requirement: A named person or team is accountable for security, has the authority to act on it, and reports on it to leadership at least once a year.

controls.title: Written security policy
controls.requirement: Security rules are written down, approved, known to staff, and reviewed at least yearly or after a significant change.

controls.title: Risk assessment
controls.requirement: Risks to the service are identified, rated and given an owner and a treatment, and the register is revisited at least yearly.

controls.title: Staff screening and agreements
controls.requirement: People with access to customer data are checked as local law allows before they start, and are bound by confidentiality terms that outlive their contract.

controls.title: Security awareness
controls.requirement: Everyone with access is trained in security when they join and at least yearly, and engineers also receive secure-development training.

controls.title: Independent assurance
controls.requirement: The provider can show a current independent assessment (certification, audit report or penetration test) of the service in scope, and lets the customer verify findings that concern it.

controls.title: Least privilege
controls.requirement: Access is granted per role, limited to what the job needs, approved before it is given, and removed promptly when the need ends.

controls.title: Multi-factor authentication
controls.requirement: Administrative access, remote access and access to production require a second factor.

controls.title: Access reviews
controls.requirement: Accounts and their rights are reviewed at least every six months, and orphaned or excessive rights are removed.

controls.title: Privileged access
controls.requirement: Privileged accounts are personal, separate from everyday accounts, logged, and used only when needed.

controls.title: Customer sign-in
controls.requirement: Customers can use single sign-on or strong passwords with MFA; credentials are stored only as salted, slow hashes; sign-in attempts are rate-limited.

controls.title: Encryption in transit
controls.requirement: All connections carrying customer data use current TLS (1.2 or later) with strong ciphers, inside the provider's network as well as over the internet.

controls.title: Encryption at rest
controls.requirement: Customer data, backups included, is encrypted at rest with current algorithms.

controls.title: Secrets and keys
controls.requirement: Keys, passwords and tokens are kept in a secrets store, never in source code or images, are rotated, and are reachable only by the services that need them.

controls.title: Data location and retention
controls.requirement: The provider states where customer data is stored and processed, keeps it no longer than agreed, and deletes it verifiably at the end of the contract.

controls.title: Separation between customers
controls.requirement: One customer's data cannot be read or changed by another customer, and the separation is tested.

controls.title: Personal data
controls.requirement: Personal data is processed only as instructed by the customer and as data-protection law requires; sub-processors are listed and agreed.

controls.title: Security in the development process
controls.requirement: Security requirements and threat modelling are part of design, and every change is reviewed by someone other than its author before release.

controls.title: Handling untrusted input
controls.requirement: Input from users and other systems is validated and encoded; queries are parameterised; untrusted data is never deserialised into live objects.

controls.title: Security testing
controls.requirement: Static analysis runs on every change, and dynamic testing or a penetration test covers the service at least yearly and after major changes.

controls.title: Third-party components
controls.requirement: Open-source and commercial components are inventoried, checked for known vulnerabilities on every build, and updated within agreed times.

controls.title: Environments
controls.requirement: Development, test and production are separate; production data is not used in other environments unless anonymised.

controls.title: Patching
controls.requirement: Operating systems, platforms and applications are patched within defined times by severity, critical issues within days.

controls.title: Secure configuration
controls.requirement: Systems are built from hardened baselines, defaults and unused services are removed, and drift from the baseline is detected.

controls.title: Vulnerability management
controls.requirement: Infrastructure and applications are scanned for vulnerabilities at least monthly, and findings are fixed within times set by severity.

controls.title: Logging and monitoring
controls.requirement: Security-relevant events are logged centrally, protected from change, kept for at least a year, and watched so that alerts reach a person.

controls.title: Network protection
controls.requirement: Networks are segmented, exposure to the internet is limited to what the service needs, and administrative interfaces are not publicly reachable.

controls.title: Malware protection
controls.requirement: Systems and uploaded files are protected against malicious code appropriate to their platform.

controls.title: Incident response
controls.requirement: There is a tested incident-response plan, and the customer is told of an incident affecting its data or service without undue delay, within the time agreed in the contract.

controls.title: Backups
controls.requirement: Data is backed up to a separate location, backups are protected from alteration, and restores are tested at least yearly.

controls.title: Continuity
controls.requirement: Recovery time and recovery point objectives are defined for the service, and the continuity plan that meets them is tested.

controls.title: Availability commitment
controls.requirement: Availability is stated as a commitment, measured, and reported to the customer.
